scope: 25 complete DE/FR/ES/JA/KO editions; bounded corrections to existing ZH/EN; Traditional Chinese derived from corrected ZH; existing URLs retained.
review_boundary: Root read all five Chinese essays; delegated reviewers read all assigned target essays against all five Chinese originals. Spanish reviewer additionally read all five existing English essays. Root verifies shared factual decisions and all final changed target-language passages before freezing.
preservation: Original Chinese and English body snapshots are immutable. Every source correction is an exact once-only replacement in batch03-source-copyedits.json. All sections, paragraphs, examples and argument sequences are retained. ZIPs and the author's external originals remain untouched.

historical_checks.topic: Grant's personal integrity, attributed rather than presented as unanimous historiography
1877 withdrawal of protection for Reconstruction governments, not evacuation of every federal soldier from the South
New Orleans: 34 Black supporters killed, about two hours
Facially neutral voting barriers are not constitutional permission for discriminatory enforcement
1883 decision addresses the first two sections, public-accommodation guarantees and remedies
Tuskegee totals count people, not separate mob incidents
EJI 4084/800 figures retained with third-edition attribution, not silently mixed with newer webpage totals
Wells and three murdered Black grocery proprietors
1887 regulatory foundations and qualified long-/short-haul rate prohibition
1882 law did not categorically expel existing lawful Chinese residents
Congressional annexation resolution and Senate treaty consent remain necessary despite executive initiative
Teller pacification exception and subsequent self-government pledge
Gates 1981 estimate: 1898–1903 war-related deaths including 1902 cholera; not a newer civilian-death consensus
Taft's constitutional/statutory authorization and reasonable implied powers
Brownsville: 167 enlisted men, discharge without honor, not a court-martial dishonorable discharge
1913 tax enactment distinguished from the Sixteenth Amendment

limitations: Targeted checks of flagged claims, not a new source audit of every historical statistic. Interpretive arguments remain the author's. Archive PDFs that could not be fetched in full were not represented as fully read; EJI third-edition figures were cross-checked against indexed report text and EJI's own webpage.
